newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BNDES confirms Brazil rail auction on Friday.
newsitem.headline: BNDES confirms Brazil rail auction on Friday.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) denied Tuesday press reports saying the auction of the southeast section of the federal railway network scheduled for Friday could be delayed.
"The auction will take place on Friday. It's out of the question to delay the auction," said Joao Carlos Cavalcanti, BNDES superintendent.
Newspapers today said the auction could be postponed due to difficulties among investors interested in the stretch to form consortia for the selloff.
Cavalcanti also said BNDES would not postpone today's deadline for investors to sign up for the auction. Bidders are required to sign up by 1800 local/2100 GMT.
So far only one group comprising transportation firms, steelmakers and mining companies has been formed to bid for the concession to operate the southeast section.
The MRS Logistica is made up of steel firms CSN, Cosipa, Usiminas, mining companies MBR and Ferteco, transport group Interferrea and other investors.
Press reports also said state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce, which was previously taking part in the MRS consortium, was seeking investors to form its own group.
Another group, led by shipping firm Grupo Libra, is reported to be in talks, but market sources said MRS was attempting to attract Libra's group to its consortium.
Cavalcanti said he was not concerned about the possibility of having only one bidder taking part in the auction.
"If there is only one group, it will be only one bidder," he said.
The 1,674 km southeast stretch, which comprises mainly track in the states of Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo, will be auctioned for a minimum price of 888.9 million reais.

Investors will be allowed to pay for the concession in 117 installments, with the first due September 27 and the remainder every quarter, after a one-year grace period, over the 30 years of the concession.
Each of the 116 installments will be adjusted by the IGP-DI inflation index. Payment will be only in cash.
The southeast section will be the third of the railway's six stretches included in the country's privatization program.
Earlier this year Brazil sold the concessions to operate the center-east and west sections.
